system_overview: This specification models the Paxos consensus algorithm, a message-passing protocol that allows a set of processes to agree on a single value despite potential failures. It is a refinement of the abstract voting-based consensus specification, adding explicit message passing between leaders (proposers) and acceptors. The algorithm proceeds in numbered ballots, each with a designated leader, and ensures that at most one value is ever chosen.
actors_and_components: The system has three types of participants: (1) Leaders -- one per ballot number, responsible for orchestrating the two-phase protocol for that ballot. In practice, a finite number of leader processes each play the leader role for infinitely many ballot numbers. (2) Acceptors -- processes that receive messages and cast votes. (3) Quorums -- sets of acceptors, where any two quorums must overlap. Learner processes that discover chosen values are omitted from this specification.
state_variables: The system tracks four pieces of state: (1) For each acceptor, the highest ballot number in which it has participated or promised to participate (initialized to negative one). (2) For each acceptor, the ballot number of the highest-numbered ballot in which it has cast a vote (initialized to negative one). (3) For each acceptor, the value it voted for in that highest ballot (initialized to a distinguished 'no value' sentinel). (4) The set of all messages that have been sent. Messages are added to this set but never removed, modeling an asynchronous network.
initial_state: All acceptor participation thresholds and vote-ballot trackers are set to negative one. All acceptor vote-value trackers are set to the 'no value' sentinel. The message set is empty.
actions: The protocol has four actions: (1) Phase 1a: A leader initiates a ballot by broadcasting a prepare message containing the ballot number. (2) Phase 1b: An acceptor that receives a prepare message with a ballot number higher than any it has seen updates its participation threshold and replies with a promise message containing the ballot number of its most recent vote and the value it voted for (or negative one and the sentinel if it has never voted). (3) Phase 2a: Once a leader has collected promise replies from a quorum for its ballot, it selects a value to propose. If any responder had previously voted, the leader must choose the value from the response with the highest previous ballot number. If no responder had voted, the leader is free to propose any value. The leader then broadcasts an accept-request message with the ballot number and the selected value. At most one accept-request may be sent per ballot. (4) Phase 2b: An acceptor that receives an accept-request for a ballot number at least as high as its current threshold accepts the proposal by updating its vote tracker to record the ballot number and value, and broadcasts an acceptance message.
safety_properties: Consistency: at most one value is ever chosen. A value is chosen when a quorum of acceptors have all accepted the same value in the same ballot. The specification maintains an inductive invariant ensuring that the algorithm implements the abstract voting protocol, which in turn implements abstract consensus. Type correctness of all variables and messages is also maintained as an invariant.
model_bounds: Ballot numbers are natural numbers, bounded to a finite range for model checking. The sets of acceptors, values, and quorums are declared as constants. The message type set includes four kinds of messages: prepare, promise, accept-request, and acceptance.
additional_assumptions: Any two quorums must have a non-empty intersection. Messages are never removed from the message pool, modeling an asynchronous network where messages may be duplicated or arbitrarily delayed. There is no need to model message loss explicitly because the safety specification only constrains what may happen, not what must happen. The specification instantiates the voting algorithm module and defines a refinement mapping showing that the Paxos algorithm implements the voting specification. A distinguished value that is not in the ballot set is used as a sentinel for acceptors that have not yet voted.
